question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Degron timing to separate maintenance from establishment
ideas.description: Add an auxin-inducible degron to endogenous Fos and JunB, then deplete AP-1 at varying times after a priming pulse. If the primed response or chromatin state is lost only when AP-1 is removed during the memory window, AP-1 is required to maintain the memory rather than only to set it up.

ideas.title: Protein turnover versus chromatin residence
ideas.description: Use Halo or SNAP tags on Fos or Jun to measure protein half-life and chromatin dwell time by pulse-chase. If the chromatin mark outlasts the protein, memory must be carried by something other than AP-1 protein itself, such as a self-sustaining chromatin state.

ideas.title: Motif-level necessity at endogenous enhancers
ideas.description: Use base or prime editing to mutate AP-1 motifs in endogenous enhancers, then track accessibility and H3K27ac through a stimulus-washout time course. Retained chromatin opening that depends on the intact motif is a direct test of AP-1 as the memory element.

ideas.title: Heritability of the primed state through division
ideas.description: Use live single-cell reporters with barcoded lineage tracking to ask whether the primed state passes to daughter cells. Combine this with AP-1 perturbation to see whether heritability depends on AP-1 itself.

ideas.title: Pulse-history and re-stimulation kinetics
ideas.description: Vary the number, spacing and interval of AP-1 inducing pulses, then measure how fast and how strongly cells respond on re-stimulation. This shows whether AP-1 encodes input history in a way that matches training-like memory, and it can be fitted to a model.

candidates: Auxin-inducible degron of Fos/JunB added at different times after a priming pulse, to test whether AP-1 is needed for maintenance or only for establishment of the memory
Halo/SNAP-tagged Fos or Jun pulse-chase to compare protein half-life with chromatin residence time, to test whether persistence outlasts the protein
Single-molecule tracking of AP-1 dimers to measure dwell times on chromatin before and after priming
Base-editing or prime-editing of AP-1 motifs in endogenous enhancers, then measuring retained accessibility after stimulus washout
Synthetic reporter with an AP-1 site inserted at a neutral locus to test whether a sequence alone is sufficient for memory
CUT&RUN time course of Fos, Jun and H3K27ac after a single stimulus pulse, tracking how long occupancy persists after washout
Time-resolved ATAC-seq after washout to measure how long chromatin opening lasts at AP-1 sites compared with non-AP-1 sites
Histone turnover measurement with pulse-labelled H3 (SNAP-H3) at AP-1 enhancers to test whether nucleosome exchange erases the mark
Hi-C or Micro-C after priming to test whether AP-1 stimulation changes 3D enhancer-promoter contacts that persist
Enhancer RNA measurement at AP-1 sites to see whether transcription at enhancers outlasts the stimulus
smFISH or MS2 live imaging of target transcriptional bursting in primed versus naive cells, to test whether memory acts on burst frequency or amplitude
Single-cell lineage tracing with barcoded reporters across divisions to test whether a primed state is heritable through mitosis
Optogenetic AP-1 pulse trains with varied number, spacing and frequency to map how past input history is encoded
Pulse-interval sweep with re-stimulation to measure how fast and how strongly primed cells respond compared with naive cells
Mathematical modelling of AP-1 autoregulatory feedback (e.g. Fra1 induction) to predict memory duration, then test the predictions with perturbations
Phospho-site mutants of c-Fos (e.g. at stability-regulating residues) to test whether protein stability controls memory length
Proximity proteomics (BioID or APEX) of AP-1 before and after priming to identify co-factors that stay bound
Fos-TRAP lineage tagging with later reactivation and conditional Fos/Jun deletion in vivo, to test whether AP-1 is required for an engram
Cross-cell-type comparison of the memory in fibroblasts, T cells and neurons to test whether AP-1 memory is context-dependent
Cross-species or evolutionary comparison of AP-1 site turnover to test whether memory-linked sites are conserved
